govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DraftMemoForBud: Draft Memo on Congressman Gonzalez: the heavily garbled draft memorandum concerning Congressman Henry Gonzalez and the House Select Committee. Damaged, but kept, complete. A single memo. From the archive shelves, for readers of the files.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GuitierrezValen:
An FBI airgram dated February 27, 1964 came from the Bureau's legal attache in Mexico City to the Director, under file 105-82555. It summarizes the travel of persons who departed Nuevo Laredo on October 3. It also covers allegations made by Ylario Rojas Villanueva.

Oswald's Mexican trip was a maze of bus rides, consulates, and border crossings, and investigators rebuilt it traveler by traveler. A summary from the Mexico City office pulled those movements into one message. The airgram preserves that reconstruction work, part of the effort to fix exactly who crossed, and when.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PiarddeDiazHort: The Miami office of the United States Secret Service kept this file, numbered CO-2-34,151, on Hortencia Piard de Diaz in December 1963. The weeks after the assassination filled the service's Miami files with Cuban names, as agents checked exile connections to Oswald. The file gives her name, the office, and the file number. It does not state why she drew the service's attention, so no reason is claimed for her here.
